simple.meaning: עִדָּן (ʻiddân) is a Hebrew word meaning “a set time ; technically, a year.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עִדָּן (H5732) appears 13 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Daniel 2:8, with occurrences in Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עִדָּן (H5732) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עִדָּן (H5732) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עִדָּן (ʻiddân) / H5732 is traced through Daniel 2:8, Daniel 2:9, Daniel 2:21, Daniel 3:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a set time ; technically, a year
definitions.full: H5732. iddan עִדָּן noun masculine Dan 2:9 time ( ᵑ7 id. , Syriac , perhaps loan-word from Assyrian adannu , fixed , appointed , or definite, time ; [Arabic probably Aramaic loan-word, Schw ZMG liii (1899), 197 ]); — absolute ׳ע 7:12 +; emphatic עִדָּנָא 2:8 +; plural absolute עִדָּנִין 4:13 +, emphatic עִדָּנַיָּא 2:21 ; — 1 in General, time , as duration Dan 2:8 ; 7:12 ; involving specific conditions 2:9 , 21 ; (point of) time 3:5 , 15 . 2 definite time , = year (as modern Greek χρόνος , see EASophocles 1173 ): ע ׳שִׁבְעָה = seven years , Dan 4:13 ; 4:20 ; 4:22 ; 4:29 ; עִדָּן וּפְלַג וְעִדָּנִין עִדָּן 7:25 (i.e. 3 2-Janyears, see Dr; perhaps read dual for plural, compare Bev Gunk Schöpf. 201 ).

occurrences.englishText: The king answered, “I know of a certainty that you are trying to gain time, because you see the thing has gone from me.

But if you don’t make known to me the dream, there is but one law for you; for you have prepared lying and corrupt words to speak before me, until the situation changes. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can show me its interpretation.”
He changes the times and the seasons.
that whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, you fall down and worship the golden image that Nebuchadnezzar the king has set up.

Now if you are ready whenever you hear the sound of the horn, flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music to fall down and worship the image which I have made, good; but if you don’t worship, you shall be cast the same hour into the middle of a burning fiery furnace. Who is that god that will deliver you out of my hands?”

it is you, O king, that have grown and become strong; for your greatness has grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth.
